10 Hotham Street
St Kilda 3002

07.08.2018

Re: Mrs Anna Jenkis, DOB 20.04.1929

Dear Dr Zeimer,

I am writing to discharge Mrs Jenkis, a patient at your surgery, who was brought in by an
ambulance into ABC Base Hospital Accident and Emergency after she had had a fall at home earlier
this morning. Your follow up on her condition would be appreciated.                                  Commented [DSM1]: follow-up


Paramedics found Mrs Jenkis on the ground slightly disheveled and unable to get up. On admission     Commented [DSM2]: dishevelled: British spelling
into A and E, Mrs Jenkis was warm, well-perfused and oriented to place and person but not to date.   Commented [DSM3]: she
Her pulse was normal, and her blood pressure was 145/80 lying and 135/85 standing. The Cchest
auscultation revealed scattered Ronchi, and an ejection systolic murmur was heard. Additionally,     Commented [DSM4]: ronchi: not capitalised
healing bruises at the elbows were seen. [Avoid ultrashort sentence] The examination was
otherwise normal; including, full range of motion at both hips with no deformities or pain noted.
Pelvis and hip x-ray detected no abnormalities except for osteoporosis. Basic investigations were
done, and a message was left on her daughter’s message bank.

I would be grateful if you could continue the care of Mrs Jenkis; including, reviewing her TFTs,
digoxin test and MSU analysis results. A geriatrics specialist review along with home help or
placement into care might be needed as her neighbours reported recent falls.

If you have any questions, please contact me.

Yours sincerely,
Doctor
